headline: Is he telling me the truth?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NO VERDICT IN EITHER DIRECTION. These three name an untruth outright, so both answers are live harms: 'he lied to you' is an accusation against a real man on no evidence, and 'he is telling you the truth' is a reassurance the funnel has no standing to give — and on this audience the second is the more dangerous of the two. 🔴 Never blame her judgment: naive, gullible, too trusting, 'should have known' are all out. 🔴 No timeframe.

Finding: she is not short of instinct, she is short of a WHOLE ACCOUNT. What she has been given covers less than what she has lived, and she has been filling the difference herself.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — his sleeve falls in heavy folds from the raised arm.
You asked about the truth of it. Your hand went to the man who chooses what to show.
So you've been given an account, dear. Not the whole of it.
And he shows exactly what he means to show, dear. No more.
But a tidy account can still miss pieces, dear.
That's why it sounds fine, dear, and something in it still catches.
Let me look closer at what stands between you and the whole of it…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — his tied foot is higher than his head.
You asked about the truth of it. Your hand went to the card that shows the other way up.
So there's another way up to this, dear. You've only had one.
And what's true from up there looks odd from down here, dear.
But two people can both be honest and still not match, dear.
That's why it stays open, dear, however long you sit with it.
Let me look closer at what keeps the two views apart…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the sun's rays are drawn as straight lines out from it.
You asked about the truth of it. Your hand went to the plainest card in the deck.
So you want it plain, dear. Straight lines, like those rays.
And nothing about him is put on for show, dear.
But what you've been handed is arranged, dear. That's the difference.
That's why plain talk feels like too much to ask. It isn't, dear.
Let me look closer at what has been bending this out of shape…
